subject: Career
title: Telling Career Stories, Not Lists
description: A 60-second lesson on Telling Career Stories, Not Lists.

hook.text: A list of duties reads like a job description. A story of impact reads like a career.

buildup.text: Each role should answer: what was broken, what did you do, and what improved?

discovery.text: This is the STAR method in miniature: situation, task, action, result — compressed to a bullet.

twist.text: Hiring managers read hundreds of duty lists. Stories are rare — and memorable.

climax.text: 'Inherited failing account, rebuilt relationship, renewed $500K contract' — that's a story.

punchline.text: Duties describe the job. Stories describe you.

quiz.question: What structure helps turn resume bullets into stories?

details.summary: Effective resumes tell a coherent career story through the progression of roles, responsibilities, and impact rather than listing disconnected job descriptions. Each position should build on the previous one, demonstrating growth and intentional direction.
details.whyItMatters: Recruiters evaluate career trajectory as much as individual qualifications. A resume that tells a clear growth story provides confidence that the candidate will continue growing in the new role.
takeaways: Each role should show progression from the previous one in narrative form
Highlight how skills built in one role enabled impact in the next
Remove content that disrupts your career story's coherence

faq.question: How do you create a career narrative when your jobs seem unrelated?
faq.answer: Identify transferable skills and themes that connect your roles: problem-solving, leadership, communication, or technical skills. Emphasize these connective threads in your bullet points so each role appears as a logical step even if the industries or titles were different.

faq.question: Should every bullet point on your resume contribute to your career story?
faq.answer: Yes. Every bullet should either demonstrate a key qualification for the target role or show career growth. Remove bullets that are purely descriptive of routine duties without showing impact. If a bullet does not advance your story, it is consuming space a stronger one could use.
